notes.title: Have You Played Tokyo 42?
notes.content:
Tokyo 42 is many things. Not as many as 42 things, because that d constitute too many things for one game to be. What it is on the surface is an isometric action game inspired by the likes of the original Grand Theft Auto and Syndicate, developed by SMAC Games and published by Frozen Synapse developers Mode 7. It s not just Grand Theft Cyber-bike, though. It s got bits of Hitman and Assassin s Creed chucked in there too, with large crowds, disguises, different enemy factions, and rudimentary platforming.

notes.title: Patch v1.1.2
notes.content:
Hey all,

We’ve uploaded a minor patch that allows for the rebinding of the Grenade-Throw key, so that those with broken middle-mouse buttons can throw grenades. There was also another bug that made the game completion percentage never reach 100% unless you’d completed Smaceshi’s castles too, which is also now fixed.

Apologies for the delay on this, and thank you again to those of you who brought this to our attention.

SMAC 
x

notes.title: Tokyo 42 only somewhat reluctantly fixes its biggest flaw
notes.content:
Hey-o. Very pretty isometric assassination game Tokyo 42 has just put out an update that aims to resolve one of the more common complaints about it – that its rather rigid camera was one of the main causes of death and/or frustration. Things’ll be different from hereon out.

Publishers Mode 7, of Frozen Synapse fame, have also explained exactly why, seven months on, they’ve kowtowed to feedback from whingey, bad-at-games hacks like me at this late stage – and why they didn’t until now.
(more…)

notes.title: Patch v.1.1.1
notes.content:
Greetings Players!

We have a new patch for you today! We address some critical issues and make some additions aimed at bettering the general game experience.

[b][u]Highlighted entities[/u][/b]

A massive part of Tokyo 42 is the isometric viewpoint and one of the more difficult issues that this creates is the way that a player can get lost behind geometry when rotating the camera. We’ve thought about this a fair deal and one of the things we wanted to try was making important entities show up as highlighted when hidden behind the world geometry.

So when you next boot up Tokyo 42, you will notice that we have done this. The player is highlighted blue behind terrain, while enemies, bullets & other projectiles are highlighted red. We’ve found that this helps the eye keep track of what’s going on, and we’re very excited to hear what you think of it.

Here's a video:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tYq-t5xuMP0&t=1s

[b][u]Bug fixes & balances[/u][/b]

We recently released Smaceshi’s castles and were very happy to see many of you trying the great lord Smaceshi’s challenges. What we were not happy to see was that some missions were actually [i]impossible[/i] to complete. We’ve now made sure that all missions are completeable, and have even re-balanced some of the more difficult ones. For this we would like to thank the community for their feedback and patience - you’ve helped us a great deal.

There were various other tiny bug fixes that have made it into this build too , some more important than others - but as always we are available here on the forums or at support@smacgames.com, and would love to hear whatever feedback you have.

Happy almost holidays,

SMAC 
x

notes.title: Tokyo 42 releases new DLC and a free charming English village
notes.content:
I’ve been calling Tokyo 42’s new DLC “Smace-shi’s Castles” in my head for the past 20 minutes now, so it’s stuck that way forever now. I don’t know what the name could possibly be referencing. The DLC adds 90 new missions, new weapons and more to the isometric shooter, and there’s also a new free multiplayer map “inspired by a village in the Stratford-upon-Avon district of Warwickshire”. I’ve popped a trailer and more deets after the jump.

(more…)

notes.title: Beautiful isometric stealth-shooter Tokyo 42's first DLC expansion is out now
notes.content:
Beautiful isometric stealth-shooter Tokyo 42 just got a little bit bigger. Its first DLC expansion, Smaceshi's Castles, is now available on Steam.

Tokyo 42, according to Eurogamer's Christian Donlan in his enthusiastic review earlier this year, "blends the original GTA, ditching the cars, with a little Syndicate and something of Crackdown in its compact, chunky, endlessly promising cityscape." He even liked it enough to pop a 'Recommended' badge on it.

Smaceshi's Castles, as its name winkingly implies, offers a series of challenges - 90 in fact - themed around Tokyo 42's core tenets of stealth, combat, and parkour.

notes.title: Patch v1.1.0 - DLC release!
notes.content:
Hello there friends!

Today’s patch is a heady mix of sweet sweet content and much deliberated balances. 

[h1]Content:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Smaceshi’s Castle’s DLC[/b] - Test your T42 assassin skills in our newly released challenge-based DLC! We’ve had a blast pulling together 90 new missions in a whole new open-world level, and are excited to hear how many of you are up to the task of collecting all of our shiny, precious medals.

[*][b]Bishop’s Itchington Multiplayer map[/b] - Tokyo 42 base game owners can take a free visit to the local pub in the West-Midlands English town of Bishop’s Itchington: The perfect place to unwind and enjoy the countryside.
[/list]
[h1]Balance:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Difficulty settings[/b] - Tokyo 42 is at times a challenging game so we decided to add some options for players who’d like to curate their experience a little more

There are 3 modes: [i][u]Easy[/u][/i], [i][u]Normal[/u][/i] and [i][u]Classic[/u][/i].

[i][u]Easy[/u][/i] mode gives the player a shield with 3 charges that act like extra lives - giving them a little bit of wiggle room after an unscheduled meeting with a stray rifle round. It also makes all of the player’s bullets a little bit faster than normal, making you more deadly than ever.

[i][u]Normal[/u][/i] mode provides only the sped-up bullets featured in Easy mode. We’ve found that these faster bullets really make the combat more punchy and fun, so this is our recommended level of play.

[i][u]Classic[/u][/i] Mode is untouched and keeps the original slightly harder T42 experience available for archivists and masochists alike.

The player can switch between these modes any time during single player play, and will have the option to choose their preference when choosing their initial save game.

[*][b]Kill markers[/b] - Feedback is such an important part of playing games, so we’ve added a little animation and sfx when you successfully eliminate an enemy.

[*][b]Aiming at ground[/b] - Rocket launchers and Heavy lasers are only truly useful when they actually explode where you want them to, so we’ve made the player aim at the ground by default when using these weapons. You can set this behaviour to be standard for all weapons too if you like, via the gameplay options menu.
[/list]
[h1]Bugs:[/h1]
[list]
[*]There have been various mini little fixes that are making it into this patch, and as always we seriously appreciate the reports that we receive in order to help fix them. So please, feel free to continue to do so either here on the forums or in a mail to support@smacgames.com
[/list]
Sayonara for now
x

notes.title: Hotfix v1.0.5
notes.content:
Hey all,

So this patch is in response to a few serious issues players have been having. Thanks to those of you who have reported these and been waiting for the fixes. We have a few things on the go here and these fixes took a bit longer than they should have - we appreciate your patience.

[u]Fixes:[/u]
[list]
[*][i]Weapon Skins disappearing:[/i] as a result of a patch pushed recently to allow players to have their skins in multiplayer, players lost access to the skins they had previously collected under certain circumstances. We’ve restored these to the player now, and if you go back into the open world you should see that your skins have all returned.

[*][i]Bike not spawning on entering the open world:[/i] The flag being checked to determine whether the player should have access to the bike was not set in time for the spawning manager, meaning that the bike would only spawn once a player did a mission with it in. This is now fixed and when entering the open world the bike will spawn under the bridge next to Yas’s bar IF you have previously completed a mission with the bike.

[*][i]LAN multiplayer is working again:[/i] some technical issues slipped through the gaps with this and have now been addressed.
[/list]
As always, thank you to our players and please do continue with the feedback and support. You can reach us either here on the discussions forums or on the support page at Tokyo42.com

Best, 
SMAC

notes.title: Patch v1.0.4
notes.content:
Hey players, we’re back with another little patch. This one is a mix of fixes and features, which is why it’s been little bit of a longer time coming.

[u][b]Fixes:[/b][/u]
[list] 
[*][i]Achievements[/i]. For many users the completionist achievement was bugged and their game percentage was never reaching 100%. This has now been fixed and will be verified when a player enters the single player open world and waitd for the game to load. Pressing ‘GO’ at this stage will trigger any achievements they are still warranted.
[*][i]‘Use’ key and ‘Map’ key binding[/i]. Previous the player was unable to map these keys to their own chosen keys. This is now possible.
[*][i]Player skins in Multiplayer.[/i] Player is now able to correctly display any skins (Cat, coat or weapon) they may have earned in Singleplayer during a Multiplayer match.
[/list] 
[u][b]Features:[/b][/u]
[list] 
[*][i]Text size increase.[/i] The text in the game has been generally enlarged to provide better visibility. This was especially an issue with players playing on a big screen from a distance.
[*][i]Multiplayer lobby chat.[/i] Players can now communicate via a chat window in the bottom right of the lobby screen. There are some known issues with the Input field losing focus when a mouse has been moved during edit. We are still looking at ironing this issue out, but wanted to get the chat out as soon as possible.
[/list] 
Okidokes, that’s it for now. As always, thank you to everyone who has provided us with feedback and please continue to do so here on the discussions page or at Tokyo42.com through our support form.

Best,
SMAC

notes.title: Balance Patch v1.0.3
notes.content:
Hello,

We’ve put together a little balance patch for Tokyo 42 single player. It became apparent to us that many of you struggled with a few of the final missions, so we went ahead and nerfed them slightly. Hopefully this will take the sting out of them a little.
[list]
[*][spoiler]Final mission: Many of the enemies in the later waves have been removed[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]Wing fight Mission: Wing’s life span has been reduced greatly[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]Alternative healing: The runners have been slowed down significantly[/spoiler]
[/list]
As well as these nerfs we’ve reduced the cost of the Cluster-chuck grenade significantly, so the ‘Weapon Collector’ achievement will be more within reach.

[i][b]EDIT:[/b] We accidentally only changed the price of the Cluster chuck grenade in one of the shop locations. The cheaper nade can be bought in the Commado's faction area (Nudist Forest)[/i]

There are some more patches coming up this week so watch this space, and as always please feel free to contact us on the support form at Tokyo42.com, or in the discussions page here on steam.

Regards,
SMAC

notes.title: Patch v1.0.2
notes.content:
Hello there,

We’re back with a patch! 

This is likely to be the last one for a day or two, but we are definitely working through the feedback we’ve received so far. On that note, thank you to everyone who is giving us their feedback and for submitting their reports of issues they’ve found in the game.

Today’s main work was put towards getting the multiplayer issues sorted, and I believe we have nailed the major one that was affecting players trying to connect to each other's games.

[b]Improvements:[/b]
[list]
[*]Region selection - Multiplayer is now qualified by a choice the region you wish to play through. These are: EU(Europe), US(Americas), and AP(Asia Pacific). I recommend choosing the region that best suits your location as the latency through the relay servers we are using can end up being quite bad if you are too far away from the region you are trying to connect to (This may in fact cause a timeout trying to join those games).
[/list]


[b]Bug Fixes:[/b]
[list] 
[*]Particular models of Xbox 360 Wireless Controllers were not properly supported before. We are hoping that the fix applied here will sort out some of the issues that some players have been having - please let us know if any issues persist following this patch

[*]Button sequences that were previously completed in a previous play session would appear uncompleted on the map when loading into the open world until they were looked at, meaning that button-hunters would sometimes think there was a button to pressed, only to become bamboozled at the lack of any actual button to press upon. This no longer happens.
[/list]
Thanks!
SMAC

notes.title: Hotfix v1.0.1
notes.content:
Hello, we’ve got a little patch here to address some critical issues.

First off, we'd like to thank everyone who has bought the game - we really hope it has been delivering some solid funtimes and brain-lovings.

Consider this one a hotfix, because there will be another one tomorrow that will fix the prevailing multiplayer connectivity issues people are having. Basically the service we are using for the connection is region locked and does not support cross-region play so we are adding a region selector in for the player to select whether they wish to play on EU, US or PA.

As for other issues you may be having, please use the discussions page to report something or go to www.tokyo42.com/support and let us know there.

[b][u]Bug Fixes:[/u][/b]
[list] 
[*]Fixed issue where collecting a weapon in a multplayer match and then going directly into single player without exiting the game first would cause the player to have their inventory overwritten with the multiplayer weapon loadout. To anyone who unfortunately encountered this nasty bug: 

[i]“You can send me your save games and I can see about getting your stuff back.

I unfortunately will not be-able to know 100% what your inventory state was from the save file, but I will be able to restore your weapon skins accurately, as well as any secret weapons you had picked up in the singleplayer.

The file is located here:

<GAME ROOT>\T42_Data\Managed\TOKYO42\<USERNAME>\T42GameSave.sav

Copy that .sav file, attach it to an email with your name as well as your loadout as you remember it before it got lost, and I will reply and get to fixing the file for you.

The address to use is support@smacgames.com”[/i]

[*]Fixed issue where steam cloud saves were only working for installs on the same windows user name. Generally this was affecting users who tried to play across multiple machines. Those users affected should run the game after updating on their original machine - the one that has the save game you wish to keep. Should you feel any save data is lost, please use www.tokyo42.com/support and cite that you are trying to retreive a lost save, they can be retrieved easily.

[/list]
 
[b][u]Environment Fixes:[/u][/b]
[list]
[*]Added a collider to a box near the entrance to the Escher maze which you could run/shoot through.

[*]Stopped civilians/enemies from pathing through the Big Tree at the Commandos forest.
[/list]

Best,
SMAC 
x

notes.title: Wot I Think: Tokyo 42
notes.content:
Tokyo 42 [official site] is a game of games. It comes across as having the pure and earnest intention to hybridise everything that has been most beloved in games from the last half-decade (and a couple from decades earlier), and then adds in cats and samurai swords for good measure. Inevitably, it doesn’t all work, but moments of half-madcap, half-measured brilliance glimmer through a patina of low-level frustration.

… [visit site to read more]

notes.title: Tokyo 42 s futuristic sneak-o-action coming May 31st
notes.content:
The stylish sneak-o-action of Tokyo 42 [official site] will arrive on May 31st, publishers Mode 7 announced today. Made by the duo SMAC Games, Tokyo 42 sees a futureperson framed for murder then try to clear their name through missions across beautiful futuristic city rooftops. It’s a looker all right, and meant to offer a fair bit of variance in how you play — Mode 7 call it “the lovechild of Syndicate and GTA 1” — from stealth to committing many actual murders to escape your murder rap.

Mode 7 say that the following trailer condenses Tokyo 42 into 4.2 seconds, which is a total rookie mistake as if you watch this you won’t need to play the game at all: … [visit site to read more]

notes.title: Tokyo 42 trailer shows different combat approaches
notes.content:
Occasionally I see some concept art for a game’s urban environment and get excited by its dramatic architecture and vibrant colours. Inevitably I see an actual screenshot for the game shortly thereafter and am immediately disappointed by the failure to translate that concept art into the actual game. I have no idea whether Tokyo 42 [official site] ever had concept art, but if it did I wonder if it was drab and plain and boring. Maybe that would explain why the game’s implementation of a city has ended up so vibrant and creatively designed.

There’s a new trailer for the isometric shooter below which walks and talks through the different ways you can approach the game’s combat. … [visit site to read more]

notes.title: Tokyo 42 - Quick Development Update
notes.content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JtiOD0GhlI0

Hello,

Paul from Mode 7 here - thought I would keep you up to date with progress on Tokyo 42.

The developers Sean and Maciek have just finished an alpha build which contains all of the main single player content: this is being played and iterated internally by everyone at SMAC and Mode 7 currently.  

There are some amazing new buildings, enemies, weapons and missions in this build that I'm looking forward to showing off when everything is completed.  You'll be pleased to hear that the variety of gameplay - from stealth to bullet-hell style action - in these missions is excellent.

They're now taking a break to work on multiplayer for a while: we should have some exciting things to announce about that soon.

Thanks for your nice comments about the game so far and I look forward to showing you more.
